name: generic methyl-accepting chemoreceptor
description: A chemoreceptor identified only by its conserved signalling architecture. It evidences that the genome encodes a receptor feeding the pathway, and nothing about what that receptor detects.

name: characterised chemoreceptor
description: A chemoreceptor whose orthology group is anchored on a characterised ligand or stimulus. Any one of them satisfies the reception function of the core pathway; Escherichia coli K-12 carries no generic-MCP orthologue and would otherwise be called receptor-less.

name: CheA/CheW kinase core
description: The histidine kinase and its coupling protein, jointly required.

name: CheR/CheB methylation cycle
description: The methyltransferase and the methylesterase, jointly required.

name: CheC phosphatase
description: A CheY-P phosphatase unrelated in sequence to CheZ, found in Bacillus and many archaea. A non-homologous replacement rather than a homologue.

name: CheX phosphatase
description: A third, again unrelated, CheY-P phosphatase family.

name: Tar aspartate chemoreceptor
description: The Tar orthologue group, anchored on the characterised aspartate and maltose sensor of Escherichia coli and Salmonella.

name: PstSCAB-PhoU complex
description: The four transporter subunits and PhoU, jointly required.
